title: Y-Maze Testing Protocol for Mice
author: Mari Golub
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yw7fxhn
materials: Select “Analysis” on the top menu bar.
Under the “Time Interval” menu, select “Full Trial”

steps.title: Prepare Testing Environment
steps.instruction: Set up the room and lighting conditions prior to testing.

substeps.instruction: Transport mice to the testing room at least one hour before testing; record transfer time and recording start time on the log sheet.
Turn off white lights and turn on four red lights (60W indirect) and the camera power strip (using Microsoft LifeCam Studio).

steps.title: Position Y-Maze Apparatus
steps.instruction: Place the Y-maze in the testing area according to specific spatial requirements.

substeps.instruction: Place the maze 2 feet above the ground in a consistent room location for all mice.
Open the Smart zone configuration file and align the maze so arms correspond to 1, 2, and 3.
Ensure arm borders do not include the shadow of the vertical wall or the last few cm at the end of the wall (mouse length) where there is shadow.

steps.title: Mark Mice for Tracking
steps.instruction: Apply markings to mice to ensure proper software tracking.

substeps.instruction: Paint a black stripe from head to rump using Jazz washable tempera paint on white mice.
Apply the same marking process to all mice in the experiment, regardless of color, if the experiment includes mice of various colors.

steps.title: Configure SMART Software
steps.instruction: Set the tracking parameters in the SMART program.

substeps.instruction: Open the SMART program and navigate to Data Acquisition > Single Subject Tracking > Configuration > Timings.
Check the 'Pre-Set' box.
Set 'Acquisition Period' to '00:08:00'.
Check 'When Programmed time is Over' under 'Stop Control'.
Ensure boxes for 'after= 1 visits to target zone 1' and 'after 1.0 sec. visits to target' are NOT checked.
Select 'O.K.'.

steps.title: Initialize Zone Mapping
steps.instruction: Load and verify the Y-maze zone file.

substeps.instruction: Select File > Open > Zones and open 'Y Maze 112114.zon' (C:\Program Files (x86)\Panlab\Smart v3.0\Zones).
Verify the zone map aligns perfectly with the apparatus; adjust the maze if not centered, but do not change the mapping.
Set 'Threshold' to '70' and 'Erosion' to '0' (adjust erosion if mice are not solid black).
Press the 'Dark Subject' button on the bottom left of the screen.

steps.title: Record Mouse Tracks
steps.instruction: Execute the tracking session for each mouse using a balanced test order.

substeps.instruction: Go to File > New and input the mouse number and date as the data label.
Retrieve the mouse from the home cage, click 'Start', and immediately place the mouse in the center of the Y-maze facing a random corner between arms.
Monitor the session quietly from the computer; if the mouse jumps out, cease the session and note it in the comments.
Allow the program to stop automatically after 8 minutes.
When the data input screen appears, paste the mouse number and date under 'Subject ID', enter your name under 'Experimenter', and select 'O.K.'
Go to File > New, select 'Yes' to save, and save the track to the project folder in 'M:\ > MBAL > Golub > Golub > Projects'.
Remove the mouse and return it to the home cage (or a clean cage if others in the group are still to be tested).
Clean the Y-maze between animals using Nolvasan and paper towels to dry.
Repeat for all mice.

steps.title: Retrieve and Export Data
steps.instruction: Generate the summary report from the recorded tracks.

substeps.instruction: Open SMART program and select 'Analysis' from the top menu.
Under 'Zone Definition', select 'Y Maze 112114.zon'.

Under 'Report Definition', select the summary report including: Trial Name, Trial Date, Exp. File Name, Exp. File Date, Subject Name, Trial Time, Trial Duration (HH:MM:SS:00), Distance in Zone, Distance in Zone (%), Entries in Zone, Resting Time in Zone (%), Resting Time in Zone (seconds), Alternation Triplet, Alternation Triplet (%), Max. Alternation Triplet, and Total Arm Entries.
Under 'Time Interval', select 'Full Trial'.
Click 'Analyze' and save the report to the study folder.

steps.title: Organize Raw Data File
steps.instruction: Manually annotate the raw data file with experimental groups.

substeps.instruction: Insert two new columns (D and E) between 'Exp. File Name' and 'Subject Name'.
Label column D as 'Treatment Group' and column E as 'Cohort'.
Hand enter the treatment group and cohort ID for each mouse.
Rename the 'Trial Name' header (Column A) to 'Test Order'.
Add the completed spreadsheet to the master dataset.

steps.title: Compute Alternation Index
steps.instruction: Manually process the data to calculate the alternation index.

substeps.instruction: Delete arm reentries (keep only the first entry of a sequence of the same arm).
Delete all entries for arm '4' (the middle zone).
Identify overlapping triads of three choices (e.g., 1-2-3, 2-3-4).
Score a triad as '1' if it contains all three arms, and '0' if it does not.
Calculate the alternation index using the formula: (# triads with all 3 zones) / (# arms entered - 2).
Ensure the denominator 'arms entered' excludes zone 4 and reentries.
